notes: Evidence-informed Bengaluru event priors. Factors multiply the normal same-weekday/time historical travel-time baseline. These are conservative priors, not measured citywide vehicle-count reductions. Strong event profiles override generic administrative holiday rules. Local procession/market effects should be applied only to affected zones when supported by advisories.

profiles.reason: Varamahalakshmi has repeatedly produced unusually light Bengaluru city traffic on the festival day, despite being administratively a restricted holiday. The previous day can be busier around shopping/market areas.

evidence.note: Reports unusually traffic-free roads; multiple commuters described dramatic reductions in travel time.
KR Market shopping rush and congestion on the day before the festival.
Documented return traffic into Bengaluru after the Independence Day/Varamahalakshmi long weekend.

profiles.reason: Dasara holidays have repeatedly produced unusually calm city roads while outbound travel rises before the break and congestion returns sharply when offices and schools reopen.

evidence.note: Contrasts unusually empty Dasara roads with heavy post-holiday traffic.
Reports easing within Bengaluru and heavy outbound holiday movement.

profiles.reason: Deepavali periods have produced very light Bengaluru city roads while large numbers of residents leave the city; outbound corridors can be substantially busier beforehand.

evidence.note: Reports ORR almost empty during Deepavali holidays and expected to fill again as workers return.
Reports unusually empty and calm Bengaluru roads around Deepavali.

profiles.reason: Ganesh Chaturthi can make normal morning commuting much lighter, while later procession and immersion activity may create localized congestion that should be handled by zone-specific advisories.

evidence.note: Reports Bengaluru roads mostly empty during the usual morning peak.
